name: Benchmark data: effect of compact data types (byte/short vs int) on procedural maze generation time in Unity
description: Measurements for the article "Optimization of procedural maze generation in Unity" (Venhlovska Y., Marchuk G., Liubchenko D.; Visnyk of Lviv Polytechnic National University, Series: Information Systems and Networks, submitted 2026). The study evaluates how replacing int fields with the more compact byte and short types in the maze cell class affects maze generation time in Unity 6000.4.3f1 (C#, Mono). Seven algorithms (Aldous–Broder, Binary Tree, Depth-First Search, Hunt-and-Kill, Kruskal, Recursive Division, Sidewinder) were run on five maze sizes from 5×5 to 100×100, 100 runs per configuration, before and after optimization (7,000 measurements). Files: two CSV files with the measurements — maze size, generation algorithm, generation time, path search algorithm and path search time (original benchmark logs with an added header row); the description of the experimental environment; an Excel workbook with the statistical analysis (descriptive statistics, Mann–Whitney test with Holm correction, Cliff's delta, bootstrap confidence intervals, model fit, memory estimate). See README.md for column descriptions.
